newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares close firmer in quiet Monday trade.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares close firmer in quiet Monday trade.

text.p: * NZ market disappoints after big Dow rise
* Telecom, Fletcher Energy, Lion Nathan stand out
* Growing focus on politics through to Oct 12 election
New Zealand shares ended firmer on Monday but failed to build on initial gains flowing through from Wall Street's strength.
The NZSE-40 capital index, which opened about six points higher, ended 7.56 points firmer at 2,221.45 after a quiet session on volume worth just NZ$33 million.
Bill Cunninghame at J.B. Were and Son said there was some bargain-hunting in both brewer Lion Nathan and Telecom, the latter also helped by a modest bond rally.

Lion firmed six to $3.65, while Telecom added eight to $6.86. Among other leading issues, Fletcher Energy climbed eight to $3.50 in further response to Gulf tensions between the United States and Iraq, even though crude oil prices have eased from last week's peaks.

Craig Robins at County Natwest said that with the company reporting season over and detailed statements released last week from Treasury and the Reserve Bank, politics would increasingly be the focus as the October 12 general election approaches.

New Zealand First, the highest-polling opposition party, earlier launched its campaign in Auckland with attacks on government asset sales and a pledge to relieve pressure from current high interest rates and a strong New Zealand dollar.

News that shareholders had approved EnergyDirect's merger with Wellington's Capital Power to form new company TransAlta NZ came after the market closed. TransAlta Corp of Canada will own 63 percent of the merged company. EnergyDirect closed one cent lower at $3.30. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
